User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the Smart Labs platform.

dateJoined.description: Date the user joined the platform.

Course.title: Course
Course.description: Represents a course offered on the Smart Labs platform (e.g., IELTS, TOEFL).

StudyPlan.title: StudyPlan
StudyPlan.description: Represents a personalized study plan for a student.

id.description: Unique identifier for the study plan.

startDate.description: Start date of the study plan.

endDate.description: End date of the study plan.

Enrollment.title: Enrollment
Enrollment.description: Represents a student's enrollment in a course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the enrollment record.

Resource.title: Resource
Resource.description: Represents a downloadable or embedded resource for courses.

resourceType.description: Type of resource (e.g., sample test, video lesson).

BlogPost.title: BlogPost
BlogPost.description: Represents a blog post on the Smart Labs platform.

slug.description: URL-friendly slug for the blog post.

content.description: Content of the blog post in HTML format.

excerpt.description: A short summary of the blog post.

image.description: URL for the blog post's feature image.

authorId.description: Reference to User (assumed to be the author). (Relationship: User 1:N BlogPost)

category.description: The category of the blog post (e.g., IELTS, PTE).

publishDate.description: Date the blog post was published.

PracticeTest.title: PracticeTest
PracticeTest.description: Represents a practice test that users can take.

id.description: Unique identifier for the practice test.

questions.description: List of question id's associated with the practice test. (Relationship: Question N:N PracticeTest)

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents a question within a practice test.

correctAnswer.description: The correct answer to the question.

options.description: The multiple choice options available for the user to select.

UserTestResult.title: UserTestResult
UserTestResult.description: Stores the results of a user taking a practice test.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user's test result.

score.description: The user's score on the test.

submissionDate.description: Date the user submitted the test.

answers.description: List of question id's that correspond to the user's answers. (Relationship: Question N:N UserTestResult)

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the Smart Labs platform, focusing on user data, courses, study plans, resources, blog posts, and practice tests. The structure emphasizes authorization independence, clarity, and security. 

**Authorization Independence (Denormalization):**

*   `StudyPlan`, `Enrollment`, `Resource`, and `UserTestResult` collections are created as subcollections under `/users/{userId}`. This approach denormalizes the `userId` into each of these documents, avoiding the need for `get()` calls to the parent `User` document during security rule evaluation. This ensures atomic operations and simplifies security rules. For collaborative entities (none are explicitly specified, but could apply to shared study plans in the future), the 'members' map approach would be used, denormalizing relevant access control data into the document.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   `BlogPost` are stored in a separate top-level collection (`/blog_posts`) to allow public access. Private user-generated content (if any) would be stored under the `/users/{userId}` hierarchy.
*   `Course` data is stored in the top-level `/courses` collection to be accessible by all users.

**Access Modeling:**

*   Private user data (study plans, enrollments, test results) is stored under `/users/{userId}` to ensure that only the user has access.
*   Courses and blog posts are stored in top-level collections to allow broader access.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

*   The structure enables secure `list` operations by segregating data based on access requirements. Listing courses or blog posts can be done securely at the collection level. User-specific data listing is secured via path-based rules under the `/users/{userId}` hierarchy.

**Example Scenario (User's Practice Tests):**

*   A user's practice test results are stored in `/users/{userId}/test_results/{resultId}`. The security rules can directly check if `request.auth.uid == userId` to allow access, without needing to fetch any parent document.  The practice tests themselves are stored under /courses/{courseId}/practice_tests/{testId} so they can be accessed to all users enrolled in a particular course.
